title: Mitochondrial HMG-CoA Synthase Deficiency in Vietnamese Patients
authors: Nguyen KN, Dien TM, Can TBN, Thao BP, Do TS, Dang TKG, et al.
population: Children from 14 unrelated families diagnosed with HMGCS2 deficiency at one Vietnamese centre between October 2018 and October 2024
funder: This research was funded by the Vietnam Ministry of Science and Technology under grant number DTDL.CN-133/21.
authorConflicts: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
result: Case series. All 19 patients had biallelic HMGCS2 variants, 7 homozygous and 12 compound heterozygous; 16 were symptomatic. First crises began between 10 days and 28 months of age, after poor feeding in 15 of 16, vomiting in 56.3%, diarrhoea in 25.0% and fever in 18.8%. During the first episode, lethargy or coma occurred in 81.3%, rapid breathing in 68.8%, hepatomegaly in 56.3%, shock in 37.5% and seizures in 18.8%; raised transaminases in all 16, metabolic acidosis in 12 of 16 (median pH 7.18), hypoglycaemia in 9 (median blood glucose 2.2 mmol/L, range 0.1 to 2.48) and raised ammonia in 5; ketonuria was found in two cases. Patient P10 presented with hyperglycaemia of 24.5 mmol/L. Avoiding prolonged fasting and giving carbohydrate during illness reduced relapses; all 19 patients were alive.
